name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.7.0 — review observation truth (2026-08-20 Salon OS field report): review-legs.js now runs the host's env preflight as a precondition before any leg, exiting 2 with stderr naming the unset declared vars and their provision commands and appending no manifest rows — closing the 3rd recurrence of the authored-not-activated class, where env-preflight.js was wired into build/design/doctor but absent from review; verdict.js's `deriveTestsSkipped` now types an unparseable skip observation as `testsSkipped: {"unavailable": true}` instead of silently deriving a fabricated `{total: 0}` CLEAN, and counts the `unavailable — skip format did not match gate output` gate row as one hard leg finding so silence about skips pages the same run it occurs — the sibling `unavailable — host runner declares no skip format` variant is a host's declared config state and raises nothing; promise-sweep.js gains an applicability cutoff (`APPLIES_FROM = '20260817'`, the date the carrier convention shipped, overridable via `--applies-from`) so specs locked before the convention existed emit a typed `not-applicable` manifest row instead of retroactive orphan noise, with undated paths applying the sweep in full (fail-closed); and a new executed producer→consumer pair test drives review-legs.js against synthetic hosts and feeds its ACTUAL emitted manifest to verdict.js, pinning the legs→verdict grammar end to end rather than against hand-written fixtures. 7.6.0 — replay scratch write access: `block-cross-worktree-writes.sh` now allows a cross-worktree Write/Edit whose TARGET tree's private git dir carries the `replay-worktree` marker AND has a `/worktrees/` segment — the mutation-authoring worker's sanctioned path into the replay scratch tree, closing the gap that had the first live run's worker blocked on Edit/Write and tunneling the same write through Bash — keyed on the target only, so a session anchored inside the scratch tree writing OUT to the main checkout still blocks, and every unmarked cross-worktree block, same-tree allow, and git/parse fail-open arm is unchanged; a same-day review-gate finding then caught the marker allow itself as forgeable — writes into a repo's `.git`-internal paths were already fail-open, so planting the marker into another tree's private git dir took two ordinary permitted Writes and no git access — closed by narrowing the marker allow to linked-worktree git dirs only (a top-level or out-of-band marker is never honoured) and by a new git-metadata attribution check that runs before the old fail-open: a target resolving inside THIS repo's own common git dir is attributed to its owning worktree and blocked unless that owner is the writing session's own tree, while a different repo's git metadata and genuine parse failures keep the prior fail-open; replay.md's Phase 1 setup gate now runs `git clean -fd` after its `git checkout -- .` restore, since checkout alone cannot remove files `setupCommand` *creates* (the same run left an untracked root `package-lock.json` that would have polluted the blind reviewer's tree) and clean cannot touch the marker living outside the working tree; and reviewer.md gains a return-contract section stating the verdict field's closed vocabulary (`CLEAN`/`REVIEWER_FAILED`) its consumers (`replay.js --score`, verdict.js) already enforce. 7.5.0 — replay first-run fixes: `--score` derives caught/ambiguous/missed from the mutation's own patch hunks instead of a single worker-reported file/line, so a multi-file mutation (the now-unbound `self-consistent-polarity` pair, which may span two File Plan files or co-locate in one) scores on any of its sites; a dismissed ambiguous adjudication now records `unresolved` instead of nothing; replay.md's Phase 1 gains a setup gate that runs the host's `setupCommand` inside the scratch worktree and records `setup-failed` on a non-zero exit, then restores tracked files before class selection; `--apply` gains a required `--patch-out` and becomes the harness's only patch emitter, under pinned git config that survives hostile `diff.noprefix`/`core.quotePath` host settings, and commits via `git apply --index` rather than `git add -A` so setup-gate churn never contaminates the diff the blind reviewer reads; `--due`/`--select`/`--stats` treat `unresolved`/`setup-failed` as non-measurement rows that never enter the catch-rate denominator or reset the due clock; `replay-corpus.md`'s `dead-wiring` recipe requires the severed value land in a consumed-but-ignored sink, never a stranded local a strict-lint gate would flag on its own.
